newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins fall, trade low as freeze unsettled.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins fall, trade low as freeze unsettled.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds fell in thin trading on Thursday as the market awaited news about whether further bonds have been frozen and readied for President's Boris Yeltsin heart surgery, which could take place as early as next week, dealers said.
Dealers said market liquidity had been much lower since Monday amid rumours some banks had been advised that some of their MinFins, totalling more than $50 million face value, had been frozen.
Officials from the Finance Ministry and Vneshtorgbank, the main MinFin depositary, have given no comments.

A banking source who works closely on MinFin market developments told Reuters on Wednesday that the prosecutor's office in Moscow's Tagansky district had issued an order to freeze almost $57 million of MinFins by face value.
"Most market makers did not quote directly today and yesterday as there is no official comments on frozen bonds," Eurobank dealer Christopher Ayale said.

Dealers said deals were struck through brokers to reduce counterparty risk in the illiquid market but the shortest three tranches, traded most actively, were finding some support at 79.00, 54.00 and 37.00 respectively.

ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer Sergei Sankov said the market was likely to remain depressed on negative news about frozen MinFins, Yeltsin' surgery and a lack of developments on plans to issue Russia's first Eurobond.
